relevance.rationale: A 2018 Sorbonne doctoral thesis on Reidemeister torsion over character varieties: chapter 2 develops the ADJOINT torsion as a differential form on the character variety, with Main Theorem 1 describing its behaviour at a finite point (and interpreting the singularities via the Alexander polynomial); chapter 3 treats the standard torsion function and both torsions at ideal points. The corpus uses adjoint Reidemeister torsion at one point only -- the discrete faithful structure -- via the Dimofte-Garoufalidis 1-loop invariant |det J_NZ| (borromean_nz_adjoint_torsion.py, whitehead_c_sigma_torsion.py, and the 2026-08-02 unified cusp law exp(2 c_0) = 2^{c-1} / |det J_NZ|). Treating the torsion as a function on the whole character variety, with controlled poles and normalization at ideal points, is the natural technique for the one honest open sub-item that audit records: the general-c derivation of the per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2}, currently pinned only on c = 1, 2, 3. That is a normalization question and this thesis is about torsion normalization -- but whether its conventions actually produce that factor is unverified, so this is new-remark, not aid-proof.

keyResults.statement: The adjoint Reidemeister torsion is realized as a form on the character variety whose behaviour at finite points is controlled (singularities interpreted through the Alexander polynomial), with a separate analysis at ideal points.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the variety-level normalization framework in which the corpus's empirically-pinned per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2} in the 1-loop cusp law would have to be derived or refuted.

proposedActions.rationale: Adjoint Reidemeister torsion is used in three corpus probes and a unified cusp law with no torsion-theory reference registered; this thesis is a citable systematic treatment.

State what would need checking before claiming this settles the open per-cusp normalization item: whether the thesis's torsion normalization on a c-cusped manifold reproduces the factor 2^{(c-1)/2} for general c, rather than only agreeing at c = 1, 2, 3. Deliberately not proposed as aid-proof.
